title: Drift Lighthouse: policy orchestrator for residency/retention with soft-remediation and audit bundles
creator: Marcus Liu
description: Build a policy-orchestration service (Drift Lighthouse) that continuously evaluates residency and retention configurations against policy-as-code, groups detections into per-tenant evidence bundles, and supports an operator-friendly soft-remediation workflow. The system must avoid alert storms by using probabilistic sampling and batched evidence delivery, produce cryptographically-signed audit bundles suitable for customer and auditor consumption, and offer operator controls for canary, audit-only, and auto-apply modes. Integration points: policy repo (git), config store (ConfigDB), console UI for approvals, and KMS/HSM for signing evidence bundles.
acceptance_criteria: Detect configuration drift for residency and retention rules across 3 environments (hosted, dedicated, private) with <= 5 minute detection latency
Produce a single per-tenant evidence bundle containing: policy diff, live config snapshot, timeline of changes, and relevant runtime telemetry
Evidence bundles are signed via KMS and stored in the audit S3 with a standardized filename and retention policy
Soft-remediation path creates a change request in the Console with suggested patch, a link to a generated PR in the policy repo, and an operator approval link
Canary rollout mode supports targeting by tenant percentage and region; default canary = 2%
Sampling and batching prevents more than one Opsgenie alert per tenant per 24 hours in non-critical drift cases
tasks: Spec: data model for evidence bundle and signing metadata
Implement drift detector for residency/retention policies (alpha)
Integrate with policy-as-code Git repo and track policy version per evaluation
Implement evidence bundler + KMS signing + S3 export
Console: approval UI for soft-remediations and change-request history
Operator controls: audit-only / suggest / auto-apply toggles and canary targeting
Create health and metrics dashboard (detection latency, false-positive rate, bundle generation rate)
End-to-end tests: simulated config drift scenarios and operator approval flow
Security review and threat model update
Run a 2-week canary across staging tenants, collect feedback
notes: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Product and Security. Decision: evidence bundles must be HSM-signed to satisfy enterprise auditors (Aisha requested signature timestamps).
2026-02-18: Architecture spike finished. Two detection modes proposed: delta-based (config diffs) and telemetry-based (runtime indicators). Agreed to implement delta-first, add telemetry rules later.
2026-02-25: UX sync. Console will show suggested patch + risk score; operator can accept, schedule or reject. Need mockups from Design (assigned DES-391).

2026-03-02: Implemented prototype drift detector for hosted region; ran against last-30-days of config snapshots, found 27 candidate drifts. False positives ~18% in alpha — tune rule thresholds and add contextual whitelists.

2026-03-05: Security review kickoff. Raised questions about KMS key access model when generating signed bundles for Private deployments. Action: add per-customer signing key alias and documented key rotation plan.
2026-03-09: Operator feedback: bundle size for tenants with heavy history can be huge. Decided on pagination + manifest summary and an option to include full history on-demand (default: summary).
2026-03-12: First PR opened against infra: github.com/redwood-inference/policy-orchestration/pull/142 — implements evidence bundler and local signer (unit tests + basic integration).
regression_risks: False positives could overload operators if sampling thresholds are misconfigured
Improper KMS key handling could expose signing keys in Private deployments
Auto-apply remediations could break customer configs if policy gaps exist
mitigation_plan: Start in audit-only mode and run 4-week observational canary before enabling suggestions
Per-tenant dry-run logs and operator approval gating for first 30 days
Require security review and per-customer key alias for signing before Private rollout
